extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and PTAB litigators (IP attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes PTAB standards and discretionary factors used in institution/denial decisions, discovery, evidentiary rulings, obviousness secondary considerations, and procedural requirements in IPRs. Useful guidance for petitioners, patent owners, and counsel litigating before the PTAB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reuse of prior proceeding expert declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a petitioner may rely on an expert declaration copied from an earlier IPR proceeding without changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board will deny institution where petitioner reused another party’s expert declaration and there is evidence (e.g., an exclusive engagement) that the declarant would not cooperate or be available for testimony; petitioner’s reliance on such a declaration can 'strain credibility' if petitioner argues the testimony was unnecessary but relied on it extensively. Conversely, reuse may be allowed where facts differ (no exclusive agreement), prior participation suggests willingness to participate, and the expert can adopt prior assertions and undergo cross-examination; normal discovery can address availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv discretionary denial factors
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board weighs multiple factors (the so-called Fintiv factors) when deciding whether to exercise discretion to deny institution because of parallel district-court litigation or other proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key considerations include proximity of the district-court (or ITC) trial date to the Board’s projected final written decision, the state of the parallel litigation (investment by parties and courts), overlap of issues and claims, whether the petitioner filed diligently after being on notice, and whether stipulations reduce overlap. The Board weighs these factors (some neutral, some favoring denial or institution) in the round.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness and timing of stipulations (Sand Revolution / Sotera / hybrid)
rubrics_metrics.description: How stipulations by petitioner to limit parallel court litigation affect the Fintiv analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Sand Revolution-type stipulation (narrow) or a Sotera-type stipulation (broader) can mitigate Fintiv concerns; a strong stipulation can 'weigh in favor' of institution even when there is a significant trial-date gap. However, the content matters (whether it meaningfully reduces overlap) and timeliness matters—an amended stipulation filed only with a rehearing request requires a showing of good cause for its late submission. Hybrid stipulations combined with evidence of petitioner diligence are particularly persuasive.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Plastic / Valve factors for denying follow-on petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria to deny petitions as follow-on (duplicative) challenges under General Plastic and Valve precedents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board examines whether the petition is a 'follow-on' by assessing relationships among petitioners (e.g., co-defendants, significant relationships), timing (whether petitioner could or should have raised the challenge earlier), whether the petitioner 'needs' to raise it earlier, overlap with prior petitions (claims/prior art/unpatentability theories), and whether a further petition would be an inefficient use of Board resources. A lack of relationship, separate accused products, different grounds, or delayed suit timing can weigh against denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joinder and 'second bite' considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a joinder motion should be granted when it would allow a petitioner a second opportunity to assert invalidity (e.g., after being time-barred or after dismissal with prejudice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board may deny joinder if joining a petitioner would undermine the finality of earlier litigation or give a party a second bite at asserting invalidity after dismissal with prejudice or after procedural time bars (e.g., under 35 U.S.C. §315(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional discovery for real-party-in-interest / privity issues
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Board will grant additional discovery to determine whether a petitioner is in privity or is a real party-in-interest (which affects time-bar and other defenses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner seeking discovery must present evidence that makes it more than a mere possibility that useful materials exist (e.g., supply agreements, indemnity, communications). If district-court discovery already produced relevant materials, the Board expects Patent Owner to show further evidence beyond speculation. The Board may grant discovery of documents related to control or funding if the petitioner indicates willingness to produce such documents (if any exist).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental information post-institution — permissible vs. impermissible
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for admitting supplemental information after institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board will deny supplemental submissions that 'supplant, not supplement' the original petition by introducing new citations and conclusions that change the motivation-to-combine or other substantive grounds. By contrast, the Board may admit supplemental evidence (e.g., exhibits) introduced in reply where the evidence reasonably could not have been obtained earlier, where it responds to new arguments raised in a reply, and where admission is in the interests of justice to allow the Board to weigh credibility and create a complete record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printed publication / public availability
rubrics_metrics.description: When documents (e.g., product manuals) qualify as printed publications for prior-art purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribution to a limited number of entities plus inscriptions and sales conditions imposing confidentiality can indicate the manuals were not publicly available. Allegations of public exposure (e.g., trade-show availability) must be supported; limited distribution with confidentiality terms can defeat a printed-publication finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant-admitted prior art (AAPA) in IPRs
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether and how AAPA can be used as prior art in an IPR proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board follows guidance and Federal Circuit precedent that AAPA in a challenged patent does not constitute 'prior art consisting of patents or printed publications' for IPR purposes. If a petitioner relies on AAPA as the basis of a ground (rather than merely to supply missing, generally-known limitations), the Board may find it lacks statutory authority to reach the merits and will not decide unpatentability on that basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to exclude for failure to produce declarant for deposition
rubrics_metrics.description: When a party may be precluded from relying on a declarant’s testimony absent cross-examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board may grant a motion to exclude a declaration if the declarant is not made available for cross-examination and the opposing party was denied the opportunity to depose the declarant. Attempts to substitute transcripts from foreign proceedings do not always cure the absence of cross-examination by petitioner’s counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary considerations / objective indicia of non-obviousness (nexus requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: How evidence like commercial success, long-felt need, industry praise, and copying are evaluated as objective indicia of non-obviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board evaluates whether the secondary considerations are tied to the claimed invention (nexus). A coextensive commercial product can carry a presumption of nexus. Evidence of copying must show reproduction of the 'entire combination of features' that were assembled. Industry praise must be shown to be the direct result of claimed limitations; marketing or advertising explanations of success require a factual showing (timing and effect) to rebut nexus or persuasiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diligence in antedating / reduction to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for showing conception and reasonably continuous diligence to antedate a reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conception can be supported by inventor testimony and contemporaneous documents (e.g., invention disclosure forms) showing each claim element. Diligence is evaluated under a rule-of-reason standard: it need not be perfectly continuous but must be reasonably continuous. Corroborating documentary evidence and testimony reinforcing periods of activity (e.g., work on figures, attorney involvement) can satisfy diligence over the relevant period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearing/changed circumstances can alter Fintiv analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Effect of changed procedural posture in parallel litigation (e.g., venue transfer, mandamus) on institution decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the facts underlying a Fintiv denial materially change (for example, the district court cases are transferred and no longer provide a basis to deny), rehearing can be appropriate and the Board may institute review despite an earlier denial tied to the prior procedural posture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory one-year deadline and supplemental trials after SAS
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether rehearing and supplemental trials addressing previously non-instituted grounds restart the one-year statutory deadline for a final written decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board has held that an initial final written decision addressing originally instituted grounds satisfies the one-year statutory deadline; subsequent rehearing and supplemental trial to address previously non-instituted grounds do not trigger a new one-year statutory deadline, consistent with Trial Practice Guide guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition word limits and revised petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of revised petitions submitted to comply with the PTAB’s word limits and whether they retain original filing dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A revised petition filed in response to a Board sua sponte order to comply with word limits may be considered properly submitted and entitled to the original filing date if timely filed. The Board may decline to expunge a revised petition if the techniques used to reduce word count (e.g., abbreviations) are not 'so extraordinary or so excessive' to justify dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forum selection clauses and institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a contractual forum selection clause justifies denying institution of an IPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A forum selection clause in a private agreement does not automatically require denial of institution; the Board may decline to deny institution even if the agreement prefers another forum—particularly where a district court denied a preliminary injunction seeking withdrawal of the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of shared suppliers / related parties on discretionary denial analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: How the Board treats arguments that petitions should be denied because petitioners share suppliers or have relationships with other petitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The existence of the same supplier or similar accused products alone does not establish the 'significant relationship' contemplated in precedential decisions. The Board looks for evidence of co-development, co-defendant status, timing of suits, and reliance on the same prior art; absent demonstrable coordination or dependency, the Board may decline to exercise discretion to deny institution.
